columns.description: Canonical asset key (BUS-204, TRAM-117, LIFT-AUB-03, TRK-T1-S07). Stable across fleet-number reissue: a reissued fleet number gets a new asset_id.
The EAM's own equipment number. Two networks reuse fleet numbers; the alias is only unique together with network_code.
Network the asset belongs to. VALMO for every row in this extract.
Bus, Tram, Bus component, Tram component, Track, Signalling, Traction power, Charging, Depot equipment, Depot facility, Stations, Systems.
Manufacturer model (Arvéa Citybus 12 D, Transalp TV-100 …).
VIN for road vehicles, manufacturer serial for equipment. Null for linear and civil assets.
Date the asset entered service. For tram TV-100 this is the 2008–09 acceptance date.
In service, Restricted, Withdrawn, Awaiting disposal.
Home depot or location (DEP-AUB, DEP-SRO, DEP-CMT, or a line segment for linear assets).
Legal owner as the EAM records it. Always 'Valmont Métropole' for biens de retour — ownership is not responsibility; see contract.responsibility_assignment.
Engineering criticality A/B/C. A = a failure removes service or creates a safety restriction.

End of this version; null for the current row.

S1 (safety/service loss) to S4.
Restriction imposed (withdrawn, speed-restricted, depot-only).
Start of the unavailability this failure caused.
End of that unavailability; null if still unavailable or not recorded.
Capital project key (P-VM-021).
Works, Equipment, Studies, Internal labour, Contingency.
Original baseline, Revised 1, Revised 2 … — each approved version is kept.
Approved amount, EUR HT.
PPI (authority), GER (Keolis, inside contract price), GRANT (state via authority).
Approval date of this version.
Role that approved the version (Comité d'investissement Keolis Valmont, Bureau métropolitain).
Project.
Forecast date. Monthly, plus ad-hoc re-forecasts.
Actuals included up to this date.
Remaining committed work — not the full PO value again.
Expected uncommitted work.
Separately held contingency (not inside the CTC figures).
Working, Board, Downside.
Controller who approved the snapshot.
Claim key (CLM-2026-Q2-02).
Project or need code the claim lines against.
PPI convention or grant agreement reference.
Amount claimed, EUR HT.
Potential, Submitted, Accepted, Disputed, Paid — five separate states, never collapsed.
Submission date; null for potential lines.
Cash received.
Supplier.

Item or service.
Ordered value, EUR HT.
Received value to date.
Cancelled value.
Date the project needs the item.

Capital project key (P-VM-021). Needs use N-VM-nnn and live in intervention_need.
Project title.
Fleet — bus, Fleet — tram, Depot & workshop, Track & civil, Signalling & systems, Power & charging, Stations & passenger info.
Need, Option study, Approved, In delivery, Commissioning, Accepted.
Operating contract the project sits under (DSP-VM-2021).
Who owns the delivery decision (Valmont Métropole, or Keolis Valmont as delegated).
Accountable project manager.
Share of scope that is renewal (state of good repair). Business purpose, not accounting treatment.
Share that is energy transition.
Share that is capacity growth.
Approved schedule baseline in force (BL1, BL2).
Task key.
Project.
Task.
Approved baseline finish.
Current forecast finish, as the project office last published it.
Predecessor task or external dependency (PO line, access window).
Reported physical progress.
Project.
Asset accepted.
Required test, certificate or deliverable.
Passed, Failed, Missing, Waived.
Accepting party.
Operating restriction attached to the acceptance.
Asset or class the assignment covers (BUS-201..BUS-208).
Owner, Operator, Maintainer, Replacement obligor, Payer (heavy component after replacement date), Approver, Handback recipient.
Responsible party.
Clause and version (Art. 34.4 / AV2).
Start.
End.
Conditions (notice within 30 days, cap €35,000, exclusion for operator maintenance default).

properties.rationale: Both carry project_code, the capital project key; a project has one budget line per cost category and version.
One snapshot per project per forecast date; the latest Working snapshot is the current forecast.
Claims to the authority are lined per project.
PO lines charged to a project are its commitments.
Schedule tasks belong to one project.
Acceptance items per project and asset.

story_group.story: Keolis Valmont operates the Réseau Valmo under contract DSP-VM-2021 for Valmont Métropole, which owns the network's assets. The renewal portfolio holds 38 projects (29 funded) across bus and tram fleets, depots, track, power and systems. A project is keyed by project_code (P-VM-nnn); a need that has no project yet is keyed N-VM-nnn and lives in intervention_need. Budget lines are kept per approved version; forecasts are snapshots with remaining committed, uncommitted and separately held contingency. Purchase-order lines are commitments, and the supplier's promised date can lag correspondence. Funding claims move through five states — potential, submitted, accepted, disputed, paid — and are never summed as cash. Assets have a canonical asset_id that survives fleet-number reissue. Responsibility is a dated assignment per asset scope and role taken from the contract and its amendments, never inferred from ownership. An open work order does not mean a vehicle is unavailable; availability comes from availability intervals.

grain.Budget_Lines: one project x cost category x budget version
grain.Responsibilities: one asset scope x responsibility role x effective period

uncertainties: responsibility_assignment.asset_scope holds ranges ('BUS-201..BUS-208') as well as single ids; the join to assets needs range expansion.
forecast_snapshot carries a Working and a Board scenario; which one is 'the forecast' is declared as Working.
acceptance_item.result 'Waived' has no rows in this extract; its meaning for completeness is not declared.
schedule_task.predecessor mixes task ids and external references (ACC-…, PO lines).
funding_claim.project_code carries need codes for potential recoveries.
failure_event.failure_mode is null on 31.6% of rows — cause not yet confirmed.

type_links.reason: Documents name projects by the same P-VM code the project table is keyed on.
Asset references in documents use canonical asset_ids (BUS-204, TRK-T1-S07).
PO numbers in documents match po_line keys.
Contracts carry the clauses responsibility assignments cite; a contract is not itself a responsibility row.
clause_ref on the assignment points at the clause.
Amendments change assignment periods (AV3 for BUS-209–216).
Amounts in documents may be budgets, quotes or claims — only the basis tells which.
A quoted amount is not a forecast snapshot.
Change requests belong to a project; the request is not an approval.
Inspections assess an asset.
An inspection finding is not a failure event.
Access requests are predecessors of possession tasks.
Conditions qualify an assignment (notice, cap, exclusion).
Organisations are parties to assignments.
Suppliers named in documents may match po_line.supplier_id via the supplier register.
People are named as project managers; personal data, masked for analysts.
A date in a document is not a schedule date unless the project office records it.
Effective and received dates of amendments bound assignment periods.
Stations and depots locate assets; no GIS to confirm geometry.
Claims are lined per project.
Acceptance items belong to a project.
Failures are about an asset.
Acceptance items name the asset accepted.
A person is not a responsible party; the organisation is.
A requested cost impact is not an approved budget line.
